$comment: Checked-in coverage map for #3802 rule 2, produced by the #3803 phase-1 audit (2026-09-30, master 1f41157ca), landed by #3802. Key = source glob relative to the repo root. Value = the formal/ families whose spec models behaviour in that file, or the string "unmodelled" for a lifecycle/timing/identity/concurrency file that no family models yet. A row is ANY-OF: a PR touching a mapped file must also touch a formal/<family>/*.tla or *.cfg file for ANY ONE of the row's families, or carry a `TLA+ unaffected: <family> — <reason>` line in the PR body for any one of them. A row listing 4 or more families (a hub file such as index.ts) is too coarse for file-level matching, so an unmet hub row prints a note and never fails. `unmodelled` entries print an advisory and never gate; they keep the gap visible. Every formal/<dir> must be listed in `families` and named by at least one row; a TLA lane that adds a family adds its row in the same PR. `notes` explains the non-obvious rows and the hot files deliberately left out. Paths were checked to exist on master at audit time.

notes.index.ts: Every hook handler lives here, so a file-level glob makes most PRs carry a `TLA+ unaffected` line. Phase 2 should narrow this row to hook anchors (session_start, session_shutdown, session_tree, turn_start, turn_end, agent_settled, tool_call, tool_result, context) once #3802's checker can match hunks, not files (#3878).
notes.clients/installer/index.ts: Only the install lock (tryAcquireInstallLock, acquireInstallLock, assertOwnsLock, the generation heartbeat) is modelled, and only partly: file-locks has no heartbeat or ownership recheck (#3553). The rest of the installer is not lifecycle.
notes.clients/lsp/server.ts: The LSP service generation (captureLspServiceGeneration, lspServiceGenerationCell, #3755) is session-lifecycle's `svc`, format-drain's ServiceGen and lsp-idle-reset's reset. The server registry table (idleEviction policy data, #3622) is not lifecycle.
notes.clients/lsp/index.ts: Per-client retirement (retireClient, #3672), capacity and idle eviction (#3622) map to lsp-crash `Evict`; per-generation derived state (EWMA, aux inflight, write-timeout streak) is not modelled yet (#3672, #3584). applyWorkspaceEdit callers are unmodelled (clients/lsp/edits.ts).
notes.clients/agent-nudge.ts: The agent-advisories store (#3757, carried on /reload by #3777) belongs to session-lifecycle, which does not model it yet. The `_touched` accumulator is unscoped (#3758 class).
notes.clients/session-lifecycle.ts: Primary/secondary classification. session-lifecycle's SecStart assumes a correct classifier; the #3662 gap classification (#3668, successor-pending marker, 60 s TTL) is not modelled.
notes.clients/dispatch/fact-store.ts: review-graph-signatures' Extract is atomic, which assumes the #3746 private-store property; the pre-#3746 shared store is below its abstraction.
notes.clients/tree-sitter-client.ts: Wasm trap budget, per-input trap entries with first-trap identity, decay on success, batch-compile keys (#3673, #3706, #3731). Modelled by tree-sitter-trap-budget (#3829).
notes.clients/fix-run-restore.ts: Whole-package fixer vs concurrent agent sibling edits: capture, the restore under pi's queue for the sibling after the target's hold is released, and the lock order against multi-path LSP edits (#3741, #3830). Modelled by dispatch-pipeline `SiblingRestore.tla`.
notes.clients/lsp/edits.ts: applyWorkspaceEdit under every path's queue (#3610) and the rename staleness capture (#3736, #3747, #3734). Modelled by lsp-rename-edit (#3826).
notes.clients/lsp-mutation.ts: LSP fallback bridge producer; carries no lineage and stays fail-open (#3763 residual).
notes.clients/mcp/session.ts: MCP session refresh calls handleSessionStart (scope 'superseded'); session-lifecycle states the MCP host is out of scope.
notes.clients/workspace-topology.ts: Marker-walk miss cache keyed by start-dir mtime plus the 2 s cadence (#3456). Low value; store-freshness could host it as a gate kind.
notes.clients/knip-client.ts: The four heavyweight analyzers stamp scannedAt at the top of their run body, before the first read (#3690); a joined run inherits the initiator's read stamp. That is store-freshness' Stamp = "start" rule.
notes.unlisted: Runtime files touched by the 151 audited PRs and deliberately not mapped (no lifecycle, timing, identity or concurrency behaviour): bounded-telemetry, cache-observability, complexity-client, dispatch/dispatcher, dispatch/types, dispatch/utils/format-utils, install-diagnostics, lens-config, lsp/config, lsp/session-roots, lsp/wait-policy/capability-snapshot, module-report, path-utils, persistent-reverify, probe-home-state, project-diagnostics/types, project-lens-config, python-environment, read-expansion, review-graph-logger, tool-agreement, tools/module-report. Also deliberately unmapped because nearly every PR touches them for non-lifecycle reasons: clients/degradation-ledger.ts (the DegradationKind registry; touched by most runtime PRs for a record kind, never lifecycle behaviour); clients/latency-logger.ts (telemetry sink); clients/hook-budgets.ts (budget table (data); #2523 governs it); clients/dispatch/runners/** (runner outcome parsing; the fix-run restore seam is mapped at clients/fix-run-restore.ts); clients/dispatch/facts/** (pure extractors; their tree-sitter trap accounting lives in clients/tree-sitter-client.ts).
notes.clients/test-runner-client.ts: Per-checkout isolation of automatic test selection (#3649). Identity keying without interleaving; unit tests suffice, listed only so the gap is visible.
